title: Glessner House, Chicago, Illinois, 1945
camera_position: Across Prairie Avenue, looking toward the east facade; inferred from the visible facade.
creator: Unknown photographer
repository: Illinois Institute of Technology, University Archives and Special Collections
collection: Office of Communications and Marketing photographs, 1905–1999
rights_basis: IIT catalog: In Copyright (rightsstatements.org/vocab/InC/1.0/). Medium JPEG publicly displayed; original TIFF marked File Restricted.
found_via: T-2199: supplied IIT lead; public catalog and medium JPEG reviewed 2026-10-09.
notes: Nearly straight-on Prairie facade: ridge caps, three stacks, eaves/gutter, corner downpipe, paired and grouped windows, entrance and boundary stones are readable. Heavy climbing vegetation obscures masonry and openings. The 1945 vegetation, paving and signs are not evidence of their 1904 state. No dimensions or material colors are derived from this monochrome view.

title: Glessner House second-floor capital with Richardson's monogram (2013)
camera_position: From the Prairie Avenue walk below, looking up at the second-floor capital.
creator: Glessner House Museum (blog 'The Story of a House')
collection: The stone capitals on Glessner House (2013-02-11)
rights_basis: Museum blog post; no licence stated.

evidence_review.date_basis: The Glessner House Museum post of 2013-02-11 shows the stone as it stood in 2013; the same post dates the carving to 1887 (carved in place from August 1887 by John Evans of Evans & Tomb).
evidence_review.reason: Close-up from the walk of the second-floor capital over the Prairie Avenue entrance: checkerboard band, Richardson's monogram in a ring, curling stems and drilled leaf tips over the dressed granite shaft. The post dates the carving to 1887 (carved in place by John Evans); nothing records a change to it, so the 2013 stone stands for the 1904 carving's pattern. The 2013 weathering, pointing and light are not evidence of their 1904 state, and no dimensions are taken from this oblique close-up; HABS sheets 3 and 6 control the sizes.
evidence_review.family_relationship: One of three close-ups in the same 2013 post, each a different capital; the HABS sheets draw the same capitals.

found_via: T-2965 (owner, 2026-10-20: 'use modern photos as needed'); fetched by kevinrhaas/chicago-images fetch-references.
notes: Close-up of the second-floor capital over the Prairie Avenue door: a cushion block under a checkerboard band, Richardson's monogram (mirrored R's on an H, boxed) in a large ring, curling stems at the sides and a row of drilled leaf tips below; the shaft's smooth dressed granite under it. The post says this is the capital over the front entrance. The post: nine capitals, front and north, carved in place from August 1887 by John Evans of Evans & Tomb (paid $1,086.50 for the carving), each different. The 2013 stone is evidence of the 1904 carving, which was finished in 1887 and is unaltered.
